chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) that Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Abu Abdullah al-Barqi, from Zakariyya ibn Imran, from Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal (peace be upon him) who said:

Nothing exists in the heavens and the earth except through seven things: decree, destiny, will, volition, writing, term, and permission. Whoever says otherwise has indeed lied about God (a) and returned [matters] to God, the Mighty and Exalted.

key_terms.أَجَلٌ: Appointed term or time of death
key_terms.رَدَّ عَلَى اللَّهِ: To return [matters] to God (implying attributing events directly to His essence without mediation)
key_terms.كِتَابٌ: The written record or book of deeds

ai.seo_question: What are the seven things through which nothing in the heavens and earth exists according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq presents this hadith as a comprehensive theological framework for divine determinism (al-Jabr), emphasizing that every event in the cosmos is contingent upon these seven interrelated attributes of Allah. This enumeration serves to refute various sects' views on free will and predestination, establishing a balanced Shia position where God's absolute will and knowledge coexist with the execution of His command. It underscores the unity of divine action, ensuring that no occurrence happens outside the scope of His decree and permission.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 7-47 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa’ed ibn Abdullah quoted Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim, on the authority of Aba Abdullah Al-Barqy, on the authority of Abil Hassan - the first (MGB) ,

“Nothing will be found in the heavens and the Earth except as a result of the following: fate; destiny; will; volition; written record; death; and permission. Whoever says anything else has indeed ascribed lies to the Honorable the Exalted God.”
